retry_probe.note: one connect-phase failure that retried through, and the report cannot say so

expect.note: only a real measurement is a completion; the phase says where the failure happened; a retried transport failure is still evidence

provenance: PR #21 review, R1 (HIGH) / R2 / R3 / R4. evals/soak.py — 206 lines producing every number in support-matrix D20 and ADR-011 Decisions 6 and 7 — had no eval case of any kind, while its sibling evals/ablation.py has three; the measured consequence is that R1, R2 and R3 were all live in a merged tree the gate scored 29/29 invariant and 93/93 fast. R1: `completed` was `[r for r in rows if not r.get('transport_error')]` and `transport_error` is only ever set on the four client-side phases, so a terminal record of `{'status': 'failure:env', 'reason': 'planner failed: ... OPENROUTER_API_KEY not set'}` — a deployment whose planner cannot start — counted as a clean completion and published `demo_ready: true`. The driver already computed `measured=is_measurement(...)`, which is False for exactly those rows, and aggregated nothing. R2: only `HTTPError` mapped to phase 2 and every other exception fell to phase 1, so a read timeout AFTER the POST landed, an unparseable body, and a 200 with no `run_id` were all reported as `1-client-could-not-connect` — the one distinction D18 and `ablation._http` are both built on (urllib wraps a failed connect in `URLError`; a read timeout raises a bare `TimeoutError`, and that run may already be executing). R3: submit and poll go through `ablation._http`, which retries connect-phase failures up to three times and neither prints nor returns the swallowed attempts, so the exact failure family the soak exists to observe could vanish and leave `infrastructure_failures: 0`. Watched red on all four halves against the pre-fix driver: phases 3/3 collapsed to `1-client-could-not-connect`, `failure:env` came back `measured=False` yet `completed 4/4 demo_ready True`, `'$39.00'` vs `'39.00'` graded incorrect, and one injected URLError left `'URLError' in report` False. Review round 2 (R11) found the repair had left R1's own shape one level up: the phase half called `run_one` and asserted only `row['phase']`, and the completion half was the only path into `summarize` — every row it built had a terminal record, so no transport-failed row ever reached the aggregator. That left `infrastructure_failures` and `phases_seen`, the two figures D20 actually headlines ("zero infrastructure failures — no transport error in any phase"), with nothing recomputing them: a `summarize` returning 0 and [] regardless of its rows kept this case green. Watched red by exactly that mutation, and by four narrower ones — each field alone, and both directions (inventing an infrastructure failure on a clean set dies as well as erasing one on a dirty set). The five rows the phase half already builds now go through the real `summarize`, and the ledger of what was excluded (`not_a_measurement`) is pinned by content rather than by its effect on `demo_ready`.

triage.note: tagged invariant — 'do not publish a green demo-readiness verdict for a deployment that never ran anything' is not a property that may regress to a baseline, and neither is 'do not name a phase the evidence does not support'. The completion rule reuses `ablation.is_measurement` rather than inventing a second one, so `failure:nav` on the live task also stops counting: that is the conservative direction (it can understate readiness, never overstate it) and it is asserted here rather than left implicit. Correctness reuses `verifier.answers_match` plus a successful status — the ablation's exact rule — because D20 and ADR-011 Decision 7 cross-compare the two figures. Every response is a stub: no network, no browser, $0.00. After R11 and R16, `infrastructure_failures`, `completed`, `attempted`, `correct`, `not_a_measurement` and `phases_seen` are graded in both directions across two reports, one made only of transport failures and one made only of terminal records; `demo_ready` is graded in both directions too, but across three reports — the same two pin it False, and the retry-probe report (a clean, fully measured, retried-through completion) pins it True, closing the gap R16 found where a `summarize` returning the constant `False` still passed. `transport_retries` is asserted by substring rather than by content; that is PR #21 R12, logged as debt, not closed here. `results` — the per-row evidence body — and the passthrough group (`suite`, `base`, `task_set`, `sequences`) are not asserted at all; that is PR #21 R17/M26, also logged as debt.
